headline: EXIRO NICKEL CLOSES VALE THOMPSON MINE DEAL — $200M COMMITTED TO RESTORE 12,000T NICKEL OUTPUT IN MANITOBA
snippet: Exiro Nickel Company Inc. closed its purchase of Vale Base Metals' Thompson Mine Complex on October 16, acquiring the Thompson and Pipe mines plus approximately 135 kilometres of exploration ground along the Thompson Nickel Belt. The consortium (Exiro, Orion, CGF) holds 81.1% while Vale retains an 18.9% minority stake alongside a multi-year offtake agreement. The new owners have committed up to US$200 million to restore production rates toward prior peak levels — Thompson produced 12,000 metric tonnes of finished nickel in 2025, up 21% year-over-year — marking one of the most significant nickel ownership changes in Canadian mining history.

headline: MONAZITE IS RADIOACTIVE ORE THAT COULD CRACK CHINA'S RARE EARTH LOCK — ENERGY FUELS THE ONLY US PROCESSOR
snippet: A Foreign Policy deep-dive on October 15 argues that monazite — a radioactive ore found abundantly in beach sands across the US South — holds the key to ending Western dependence on Chinese rare earth processing. Energy Fuels is currently the only US entity legally permitted to process monazite at its White Mesa Mill in Utah, having produced its first batch of 99.9%-pure terbium oxide in March 2026. A Phase 2 expansion would scale monazite intake from 10,000 to 60,000 metric tonnes per year, positioning Energy Fuels as the one company that could supply the entire US-EU midstream rare earth gap without a single tonne of Chinese material.

headline: SSR MINING BIDS C$6.75/SHARE FOR ROXMORE'S 5.2M-OZ NEVADA GOLD — $200M SYNERGIES SEEN WITH MARIGOLD
snippet: SSR Mining (TSX: SSRM) announced a C$6.75 per share all-cash offer for Roxmore Resources on October 13, a 27% premium to the prior close, valuing the deal at approximately $464 million in equity (or C$712 million including a concurrent exploration company spinout). The Converse project sits 6 kilometres from SSR's Marigold complex in Nevada and holds 103 million tonnes of indicated resources at 0.65 g/t gold (2.2 Moz) plus 218 million tonnes of inferred at 0.43 g/t (3.0 Moz); SSR projects at least US$200 million in life-of-mine synergies with Marigold targeting 150,000–170,000 ounces annually starting around 2033.

headline: TRUMP SONS BACK KAZAKH TUNGSTEN DEAL WITH $1.6B US GOV'T SUPPORT — KAZ RESOURCES WOULD CONTROL 15% OF GLOBAL OUTPUT
snippet: IntelliNews confirmed that Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump hold a stake in Skyline Builders Group, which is merging with Cove Kaz Capital to form Kaz Resources (Nasdaq: KAZR). The combined entity would control the Northern Katpar tungsten resource in Kazakhstan — 1.4 million tonnes of tungsten trioxide at roughly 12,000 metric tonnes per year, or approximately 15% of current global production — backed by Letters of Interest from US Ex-Im Bank ($900M) and the Development Finance Corporation ($700M). An October 12 update confirmed site preparation and drilling underway at Northern Katpar; the merger remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approval expected Q4 2026–Q1 2027.

headline: NICKEL SLIDES TO 9-MONTH LOW AT $15,252/T — LME STOCKS SWELL TO 283,000 TONNES AS INDONESIA WEIGHS SMELTER MORATORIUM
snippet: Nickel fell to $15,252 per tonne on October 16, its lowest since late 2025, as LME warehouse inventories near 283,000 tonnes and a strengthening US dollar reinforced persistent oversupply. Indonesia — responsible for roughly 55% of global nickel mine supply — is weighing a moratorium on new smelters producing semi-finished nickel products to address an estimated global surplus of 2.5 million tonnes; any formal announcement would be the most significant Indonesian supply-side intervention since the January 2020 ore export ban and could be the catalyst needed to stabilize nickel equities.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD-OIL RATIO NOW BEARISH FOR MINING STOCKS — NFTRH'S TANASHIAN WARNS CORRECTION NOT YET COMPLETE
snippet: In his October 15 NFTRH market update published on GoldSeek, analyst Gary Tanashian argues the gold-to-oil ratio has shifted into territory that is historically bearish for mining equities — a leading indicator he identifies that mining stocks tend to discount before broader sentiment catches up. Tanashian also flags an expected period of yield-curve flattening that he characterizes as a Goldilocks scenario — favorable for the economy but typically unfriendly for gold — and concludes that mining stocks are already pricing this dynamic even as spot gold holds support above $4,100.

headline: COBALT FALLS TO $17.85/LB AS LFP BATTERY CHEMISTRY DISPLACES NMC — 1-MONTH DROP OF 7.4%
snippet: Cobalt prices fell to approximately $17.85 per pound ($39,245/tonne) around October 14, down 7.4% over the preceding month and roughly 8% year-over-year, as the continued industry shift toward LFP battery chemistry — which uses zero cobalt — structurally erodes demand. China's domestic benchmark diverges significantly from Rotterdam warehouse prices, with the gap widening in 2026 as CATL and BYD accelerate LFP deployment in mass-market EVs. For junior cobalt producers on the TSX-V, the disconnect between current prices and the $35,000-plus marginal cost floor for most DRC operators continues to compress project economics.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,100 FLOOR — OCT 27-28 FOMC THE NEXT TEST AS SECOND RATE HIKE IN CYCLE SEEN 50/50
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's October 2026 gold price forecast identifies the October 27-28 FOMC meeting as the key binary event for precious metals through year-end, placing the base case for a breakout at $4,200–$4,400 if PCE data and jobs numbers do not force the Fed's hand. Gold briefly violated $4,086 during the October 14 CPI shock before recovering to $4,177 on October 16 — a V-shaped test of the $4,100 floor that bulls need to hold. The September 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%, the first in the current cycle, has futures markets pricing the next meeting at approximately 50/50 for a second hike.

headline: CANADIAN FIRM U92 DEFENDS CONTROVERSIAL URANIUM EXPLORATION IN GUYANA — LICENCES COVER URANIUM AND RARE EARTHS THROUGH 2029
snippet: Canadian junior U92 issued a public defence of its uranium exploration programme in Guyana on October 16, amid local opposition to its licences covering uranium, radioactive minerals, and rare earth elements in the country's interior. The licences run through April 2027 with options to extend for up to two additional one-year periods to 2029 — a frontier jurisdiction that U92 argues could become a new non-Russian, non-Kazakh source for nuclear utilities seeking to diversify supply chains. The story represents the growing push into politically complex jurisdictions as tier-1 uranium exploration ground becomes increasingly contested.

headline: CONTRARIAN: GOLD H&S PATTERN TARGETS $3,920 AND GDXJ BELOW $100 — ANALYST SAYS TECHNICAL SETUP STILL VALID
snippet: A technical analysis by goldpriceforecast.com identifies an active head-and-shoulders pattern in gold whose measured downside target extends near $3,920 — just below the $4,000 support zone that was briefly breached during the October 14 CPI selloff before recovering. The corresponding GDXJ target is placed slightly below $100, and the analyst argues the pattern remains valid unless gold achieves a sustained close above $4,350. Published as a counterpoint to the predominantly bullish consensus, the piece frames the October 14 bounce as a dead-cat test rather than a confirmed reversal, with the FOMC outcome on October 27-28 as the decisive trigger.
